evidence: Single codebase with clear package/module boundaries: trackeval/, scripts/, tests/, datasets/, metrics/, baselines/
Central core (trackeval) with well-defined layers: datasets and metrics both inherit from abstract base classes (_BaseDataset, _BaseMetric), indicating separation of concerns and dependency inversion
Script-based entry points (scripts/*.py) that import from the core library — typical of modular monoliths where CLI tools call reusable core modules
No external service communication patterns; all functionality is within one Python package
High average fan-out (5.1) indicates modules depend on many others, consistent with cohesive monolithic architecture rather than microservices or hexagonal (which would enforce stricter isolation)
Package structure matches standard Python modular monolith: shared utilities (utils.py), domain models (datasets, metrics), and adapters (baselines)
Minimal coupling: each dataset and metric implements interface and imports only from core (no cross-dataset/metric dependencies)
risks: Tight coupling between modules (high fan-out) may reduce testability and modularity over time
Shared imports (e.g., multiple modules importing from . import utils) could create circular dependencies if unmanaged
No explicit dependency injection pattern; configuration via dict-like defaults (init_config) could reduce flexibility in complex deployments
